The characteristic of a ring is the smallest positive integer \(n\) such that \(n \cdot a = 0\) for all elements \(a\) in the ring. If no such \(n\) exists, the characteristic is 0.

- For \(\mathbb{Z}_3\) (integers modulo 3), the characteristic is 3.
- For \(3\mathbb{Z}\) (the set of multiples of 3 in \(\mathbb{Z}\)), there is no positive integer \(n\) such that \(n \cdot b = 0\) for all \(b \in 3\mathbb{Z}\), because \(n \cdot (3k) = 3nk\) is zero only when \(n = 0\). Thus, the characteristic of \(3\mathbb{Z}\) is 0.

The characteristic of the direct product ring \(\mathbb{Z}_3 \times 3\mathbb{Z}\) is the least common multiple of the characteristics of its factors. Since one factor has characteristic 0, the product has characteristic 0.
